title: Lookup from the Search State
statement: Let $mode$ be a Boolean mode, let $w,b,b'$ be bit strings, let $q$ be a natural number, and let $v$ assign natural numbers to the nine registers. Suppose every register value is at most $4|\langle\langle\langle w,b\rangle,b'\rangle,\mathrm{bits}(q)\rangle|+4$, and the registers satisfy $v(0)=0$, $v(5)=4(2|w|+2)$, $v(3)=4|\langle w,b\rangle|+4$, $v(2)=4|\langle w,b\rangle|+4+2|b'|$, $v(6)=q$, and $v(7)=0$. Starting on input $\langle\langle\langle w,b\rangle,b'\rangle,\mathrm{bits}(q)\rangle$ in state $seek(false)$ with values $v$ and no answer, the machine halts with the test $q<|dropIdx(\langle\langle w,b\rangle,b'\rangle)|$ when $mode$ is true, and otherwise with the bit of that decoded string at position $q$, defaulting to false when out of range. Every configuration before halting satisfies the machine's safety condition and register bound.
hypotheses_covered: mode is a Boolean machine mode
w, b, and b' are bit strings
v assigns natural-number values to the nine registers
every register is bounded by four times the encoded input length plus four
